feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Corrected direction: the earlier records had accelerator:pep-ii feeding accelerator:slac-linac, which reversed the chain. The linac supplied PEP-II with 9.0 GeV electrons and 3.1 GeV positrons (full-energy injection through the injection beamlines in the linac housing). No dates: the relationship runs over PEP-II's operation (hull of the two records, 1999 to 2008). SLAC says the linac was "linac-driven" for a series of three colliders, PEP, SLC and PEP-II (SLAC, 2016).
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: Utilization of the existing high power, low emittance beams available at SLAC required that a great portion of the systems for pulsed extraction and transport of 9.0 GeV electrons and 3.1 GeV positrons for injection into the PEP-II rings will reside in the existing linac housing.

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: SLAC news item "SLAC's Historic Linac Turns 50 and Gets a Makeover", section on the linac's discoveries; SLAC graduate handbook page; SLAC Milestones, 1990
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start: 1972, SPEAR's first year (the handbook: "With the advent of colliding beam storage rings (SPEAR in 1972) and PEP (in 1980), which are discussed in more detail below, the SLAC linac also served as source and injector for electrons and positrons."). End: 1990, when SPEAR became a dedicated synchrotron-radiation facility with its own injector (SLAC Milestones: "1990: SPEAR becomes a dedicated synchrotron radiation facility with its own independent injector."; the handbook: "The SPEAR storage ring now has its own electron injector (linac and synchrotron booster)."). Year precision; the end is inferred from the change of injector.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: In 1972, the linac beams were for the first time injected into the SPEAR storage ring to produce exotic new particles in powerful electron-positron collisions.

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: SLAC graduate handbook page, "The Linac and the SLAC Linear Collider"; SLAC news item; SLAC Milestones, 1980; CERN Courier, "SLAC at 50"
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start: 1980, when PEP began operating (SLAC Milestones: "1980: PEP operations begin"); the 2016 SLAC news item calls PEP one of "three linac-driven particle smashers" from 1980 to 2008. End: 1990, the end of PEP's collider running (CERN Courier: "ran during the years 1980–1990"); the PEP ring was later reused as the high-energy ring of PEP-II, which the linac also fed (the existing accelerator:pep-ii link). Year precision.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: With the advent of colliding beam storage rings (SPEAR in 1972) and PEP (in 1980), which are discussed in more detail below, the SLAC linac also served as source and injector for electrons and positrons.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: SLAC news item, "SLAC's Historic Linac Turns 50 and Gets a Makeover", section "50 Years of Discovery"
intervals.note: First particle beam, 21 May 1966; "completed in 1966" on the SLAC handbook page. Since 2009 one-third of the copper linac has driven the LCLS X-ray laser and the first third was cleared for LCLS-II; FACET, which used the first two-thirds, shut down on 4 April 2016 (same item).
intervals.quote: When the linac produced its first particle beam in the early morning hours of May 21, 1966, it was the single largest civilian science project ever undertaken by the U.S. government.

name: SLAC linear accelerator
notes: The linac has fed SPEAR (from 1972) and PEP (1980-1990), both linked here since 2026-10-26 (follow-ups 2); PEP-II (1999-2008) is linked here; LCLS has no record. The SLC (1989-1998) did not take beam from the linac: "Starting in 1983, extensive modifications and additions to the existing linac enabled it to simultaneously accelerate and collide 50 GeV electrons and positron bunches" (SLAC handbook page), so the linac was the SLC's accelerator, and no feeds relationship is recorded.

beam_energy.locator: SLAC graduate handbook page, "The Linac and the SLAC Linear Collider"
beam_energy.note: Maximum, after the 1980s klystron upgrade; originally "electron beams of about 20 GeV and positrons of about 13 GeV", above 30 GeV after SLED in the 1970s (same page). The linac is shared: PEP-II used it at 9.0 GeV (electrons) and 3.1 GeV (positrons).
beam_energy.quote: In the 1980s, new, improved klystrons manufactured at the laboratory reached peak powers of 64 MW which, in combination with SLED, boosted the linac energy to 50 GeV.

length.locator: SLAC graduate handbook page, "The Linac and the SLAC Linear Collider"
length.note: Derived by unit conversion: SLAC states "two-mile-long" (the 2016 news item says "2-mile-long linac"); 2 mi x 1.609344 km/mi = 3.22 km.
length.quote: The first major accelerator facility at SLAC was the two-mile-long linear accelerator, completed in 1966.

summary.plain: SLAC's two-mile-long linear accelerator, which fires electrons (and, in its early years, positrons) down a straight underground tunnel. It has fed three generations of SLAC's experiments: the original fixed-target program, the SLC and PEP-II colliders, and today the LCLS X-ray laser.
summary.technical: The 3.2 km SLAC linear accelerator (operating since 1966), capable of up to 50 GeV for electrons; the accelerator of the Stanford Linear Collider (1989-1998), injector for the PEP-II B-factory (1999-2008), and also feeds the LCLS free-electron laser, which has no accelerator record in the Atlas.
